supersedes_reason: adds ceilings: each scene's own global curve and own local table, and the shared curve with a per-scene gain and zone shift fitted on pixels (v001: degenerate gain test)
question: What explains Lightroom Highlights beyond the pixel luminance?

method.input: Lightroom pairs neutral -> Highlights variant, pixel-aligned
method.effect: e = log2(Y1 / Y0), Rec.709 luminance of linear sRGB
method.explanatory: per scene RMS of e around its median per predictor bin (empty 2D cells: 1D median)
method.predictive: leave-one-scene-out mean of per-scene tables; y * 2^(g L), clipped at 1
method.gain: g = 1, or least squares of e on L over all valid pixels of the scene
method.criterion: mean sRGB-encoded Y of the 10 % brightest neutral pixels, prediction / LR - 1
method.ceilings: own_<predictor>: the scene's own median table applied to itself (best curve of that form for the image); shared_Y_gain_shift: leave-one-out shared curve, gain and zone shift (-3..+3 EV) fitted on the scene's pixels by least squares

limits: Simulated on the LR neutral: isolates the operator, not IPR's development
Luminance effect only; colour handling (darkenKeepingColour) not modelled
The pixel gain is fitted on the scene itself: an upper bound for a gain predictor
Two-dimensional tables have more cells: compare predictive results, not only RMS
Analysis at 1/8 resolution: detail finer than 8 px is not assessed
